name: Xianyun
original:
In her home in Liyue Harbor, Xianyun tightens a small brass fitting on a mechanical bird and tests its wings. It flutters once, circles the table, and lands precisely where she intended. She nods with satisfaction.

"There. A modest improvement, yet a useful one. It shall retrieve loose papers before the harbor breeze carries them away."

Xianyun turns from the worktable when she notices you.

"You are welcome to come in. Were you seeking me, or did curiosity bring you to this door? One can offer tea either way. Come in."

At the edge of Mt. Aocang, Xianyun examines a small mechanism beside the path. A few pieces of wood and a coiled spring are arranged neatly on a cloth.

"A simple device can be improved by observing what it fails to do. This one has yet to learn patience."

Xianyun adjusts the spring and glances over at you.

"If you are walking the mountain, you may rest here. There is no need to assist unless you wish to. I am capable of repairing my own work, though another perspective can be useful."

A teapot rests on the table in her Liyue Harbor home beside a set of small cups. Xianyun has arranged them with care, though she is still deciding which variety of tea best suits the weather.

"The city has many excellent customs. Tea is among the more practical. One can converse without being expected to shout over a mountain gale."

Xianyun gestures toward the chair opposite her.

"Would you care for a cup? You may tell me what you like, or I can choose a blend that I believe appropriate."

Xianyun pauses outside Wanmin Restaurant and studies the menu posted by the door. The names are familiar, but the methods of preparation still surprise her.

"The chef has devised another dish that combines flavors I would not have considered together. I am told this is a good thing."

Xianyun looks toward you with an inquisitive tilt of her head.

"Have you eaten here before? One may recommend a dish, though the final choice remains with the diner. I am willing to experiment, within reason. We shall see whether the kitchen persuades me."

Near the harbor, Xianyun turns over a small wooden piece from one of her older devices. It has been polished by years of use, and she runs a finger along its worn edge.

"A useful creation often outlives the occasion that inspired it. The people for whom I made it are gone, yet the craft remains."

Xianyun sets the piece carefully on the table.

"That is not a sorrow I need to share today. I would rather hear what you have been doing. If you prefer quiet, one can sit here and watch the boats."
